Name: ASTRA E.V.
Company description: About our current project - "𝙋𝙧𝙤𝙟𝙚𝙘𝙩 𝙆𝙖𝙧𝙢𝙖𝙣",       To date, there are no student groups within Europe that have successfully designed, built, and launched a rocket that has reached space (100 km altitude).  Reaching the Karman line (the boundary of space) is generally regarded as the first step to developing launch system technologies and serves as a good platform from which to understand the technical challenges involved in building orbital launchers, which is a field that is currently expanding exponentially.        The ongoing mission of 𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔 (Association for Space Technology and Research Applications) is to provide an opportunity for students of the University of Bremen to engineer and innovate in a capacity that complements their programs. The primary goal of the project is to design, build, and launch a rocket to reach an altitude of 100 km. This project shall serve as a technology demonstrator and engineering exercise to enhance the quality of education at the University of Bremen through the availability of hands-on experience for the student body and inspire the student community.  If successful, this vehicle could serve as a platform to launch future scientific payloads requiring 5-10 minutes of microgravity.

Company description: iwiation GmbH provides expert assessments in the area of accident reconstruction and visualisation.  Witness and video footage can be essential, if flight data is not available or radar data is not complete / insufficient accuracy due to terrain reflection.  The world-wide unique method called Immersive-Witness-Interview (iwi®) was developed to reconstruct missing data based on eyewitness statements and / or video information for flight path reconstruction. Flight path and aircraft attitude data can be reconstructed based on available witness / video information. The reconstructed accident scenario can become quickly complex and visualization can be essential to provide material for documentation, analysis and explanation, how the accident occurred. Further, more and more accidents are related to human factors. Therefore a photorealistic real-time visualization can support to better understand the reconstructed accident scenario from different perspectives. Root causes like weather conditions, mission, reaction time, diversion, etc. can be analyzed with the developed Virtual-Reality environment. To do so, the reconstructed flight path and the overall accident scenario including terrain, aircraft geometry and cockpit instrumentation are transferred into Virtual-Reality, providing a real-time and photorealistic rendering. This can be used by authorities during the analysis of the accident sequence and dedicated scenes can be documented in the final report. The integrated eyetracking technology allows detailed human factor analysis of accident sequence playback. The results can be used by operators for lessons learned training to further improve aviation safety.
